pundit.name: Landon Donovan
pundit.take: **Look, I get why people think Gunner is leading this pool, but let's not pretend it's anything more than blind luck at this point.** Sure, his roster includes France, a powerhouse in Tier 1, but anyone who drafts DR Congo in Tier 4 is clearly throwing darts while wearing a blindfold. I feel for Devin, I really do—especially after weathering the emotional rollercoaster of Spain's unpredictable form—yet when you watch him draft Haiti in the fourth round, you can't help but question if he's a little too attached to the underdogs. On the other hand, Gayden, the self-proclaimed "Backpass Assassin," might as well be passing his remaining hopes backward with Korea Republic, who aren't exactly setting the world alight. But let's not forget about Zach, or "Mustard Boy" as he'd like us to call him, languishing at fourth with a roster that, on paper, should have done better. If you're relying on Saudi Arabia for advancement points, you might as well start training as a mustard sommelier. And bless his heart, young Rafe, or "The Noisemaker," is clearly learning the harsh reality that not all chaos leads to glory—especially when Germany's inconsistency leaves him clinging to the fantasy equivalent of a sinking ship. As we move forward, the schadenfreude is palpable; the only certainty is that the near future is bound to unravel spectacularly for at least one of these bold strategists.
